requirement:
Under `confirm`, a first `false` MUST finish the round for that subject. After
`true` or FIXME, the harness MUST obtain exactly one independent second assessment
of the same subject, with the same mandatory inputs and source state. Each
assessment may discover additional inputs and has its own usage record under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.usage_storage`.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.authoring.confirmation` has no structural obligations that need implementation evidence. I checked each clause for an alternative implementation that keeps the same observable behavior but breaks the clause.

- "a first `false` MUST finish the round for that subject": this is a control-flow outcome. A state machine, an early return or a loop break would all produce it. No type, library or interface is named.
- "After `true` or FIXME, the harness MUST obtain exactly one independent second assessment": this specifies how many assessments run and when. The harness could start the second assessment from a function, a subprocess or a queue and behave the same way. "Independent" describes the result. The second assessment must not depend on the first one's output, however the code is arranged. It does not prescribe a mechanism.
- "of the same subject, with the same mandatory inputs and source state": this is a data-equivalence requirement on what the second assessment sees. The harness could meet it by recomputing the inputs or by reusing a snapshot. Either way the second assessment sees the same inputs.
- "Each assessment may discover additional inputs": this is a MAY, so it imposes nothing to check.
- "has its own usage record under {cite}`requirements.authoring.usage_storage`": this is a citation, so it supplies context only. The record's format and location are obligations of `requirements.authoring.usage_storage`, which would be judged under its own text.

Every clause describes observable behavior. The behavior is the count and ordering of assessments, the identity of their inputs, and the existence of per-assessment usage records. No signature, field, algorithm, library or named delegation is prescribed. Behavioral evidence from tests covers it. The empty root list is therefore consistent with the requirement.

behavioral: The tests cover each obligation in `requirements.authoring.confirmation`. I judged this from the supplied test source only. I did not request implementation source.

**A first `false` finishes the round.**
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[without_confirm_or_after_a_false_judgment_one_assessment_is_recorded]` runs a `false` first judgment under confirm. It asserts exactly one provider request, one usage log, and that the recorded rationale is the first one ("A gap.").
- It also checks that a `true` judgment without confirm produces one assessment.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[adaptive_sol_failure_is_final_and_confirm_selects_the_failed_assessment]` is the only other test that touches this case, and it exercises adaptive routing. It does not independently pin down the single-assessment behavior.

**After `true` or FIXME, exactly one independent second assessment.**
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[agreeing_assessments_record_the_first]` uses a FIXME first judgment under confirm. It asserts exactly two prompts and two usage logs, and that `prompts[0] == prompts[1]`. That equality covers the same mandatory inputs and source state, and the same initial prompt and tools.
- The same test asserts that the two conversations are separate, with their own usage records labelled `requirements.ready` and `requirements.ready (second assessment)`.
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[confirm_runs_a_second_assessment_with_its_own_usage_record]` is an end-to-end run with a `true` outcome. It asserts exactly two requests, both for the same subject. It also asserts two usage records, one of them a "(second assessment)" record.
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[confirm_with_all_runs_a_second_assessment_for_each_batch_subject]` and `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[policy_comes_from_the_flag_then_the_configuration_then_defaults_to_confirm]` check that the count is exactly two under confirm (versus one under once) and that every conversation has its own usage record.
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citation_reviews_are_confirmed_with_fresh_targeted_conversations]` covers citation subjects. It asserts that the second conversation targets the same item, that it does not contain the first rationale, and that there are two distinct run ids.
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[structural_assessments_and_confirmation_use_the_same_structural_contract]` covers the structural and behavioral criteria. Each confirmation conversation is checked for the same inputs, and the first result's rationale is checked to be absent from the later prompts.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[adaptive_routes_fresh_assessments_and_records_each_model]` asserts that each conversation is fresh (a single input element). It also asserts that the first rationale is not leaked, that run ids are distinct, and that each assessment has its own usage log.

**Each assessment may discover additional inputs and has its own usage record.** Separate usage records are asserted in all of the tests above. The discovery of additional inputs is a permission ("may"), so it imposes nothing to check. The separate record format itself is governed by `requirements.authoring.usage_storage`, which is cited rather than reassessed here.

**Related behavior.**
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[disagreeing_citation_assessments_record_both_explanations]` and `src/commands.rs#mod[tests]/fn[status_lists_definitions_and_reviews_whose_assessments_disagreed]` cover how disagreement is recorded and reported. That behavior is outside this requirement's text and is not needed for adequacy.

No behavioral obligation is left untested.

text: :::{req} confirmation
Under `confirm`, a first `false` MUST finish the round for that subject. After
`true` or FIXME, the harness MUST obtain exactly one independent second assessment
of the same subject, with the same mandatory inputs and source state. Each
assessment may discover additional inputs and has its own usage record under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.usage_storage`.
:::{req} usage_storage
Each assessment MUST have a separate JSON usage record under
`<state-root>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json` using
{cite}`requirements.configuration.state_location`.
It MUST identify its format version, run, project root, subject kind and full
name, start time, backend and model when known, end time when finished, outcome,
accepted determination kind (`true`, `false`, or `FIXME`) when present, and
whether evidence was written. It MUST record the selected output destination in
`evidence_output` as `file` or `stdout`; a successful write to either destination
MUST set `evidence_written` to true. Usage recording MUST remain outside the
project in stdout mode. FIXME entry text MUST NOT be stored in usage records.
Failed, cancelled, or unfinished
runs MUST remain distinguishable from completed judgments. Records MUST persist
for later review without storing source text, prompts, responses, or rationale.
